articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Browns have kicked off against the Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) on "Thursday Night Football."

Deshaun Watson's late-game performances and the Browns' 2-1 start mean Cleveland entered the game with first place in the AFC North on the line.

With a 13-6 record in Thursday games, Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers headed into the Week 4 matchup tied with Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for the second-most wins on Thursday in the Super Bowl era. The only person in front of him? Tom Brady with 14, meaning Rodgers can move into a tie for first place with a win in Cleveland.

articles.headline: How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict
articles.description: As the reaction to Man City's guilty verdict continues to ripple across the sporting world, the club's internal messaging is very much one of confidence and carrying on. That may be easier said than done.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティの選手やスタッフはプレミアリーグの有罪判決にどう対処しているのか
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティに対する有罪判決の反響がスポーツ界全体に広がり続ける中、クラブ内部のメッセージは「自信を持って平静を保つ」という姿勢です。しかし、それは言うほど簡単ではないかもしれません。
articles.body:
The strength of the judgment against Manchester City, following their legal case with the Premier League, has shocked the club, its employees and their players. Most of those inside the City Football Academy (CFA) accept that the verdict -- made public for the first time Tuesday -- is a worst-case scenario.

There has been speculation and discussion on and off at the CFA for more than three years since the charges were announced in February 2023 about what might happen. It was always viewed internally as highly unlikely that every count of financial misconduct would be proved.

City insist they are innocent -- a message that has come from the top, namely chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and CEO Ferran Soriano -- and many employees want to give the club the benefit of the doubt. They enjoy working for City and feel that they've been well looked after over the years.

In that respect, many people ESPN spoke with for this story are choosing to believe Al Mubarak and Soriano. At the very least, the majority of these staff members are prepared to wait until after the appeal is heard before passing judgment.

- Legal explainer: Man City have been charged. Now what?

- Marcotti: Hard to see how Man City come back from seismic scandal

- Ogden: Does Man City's guilty verdict ruin Guardiola's legacy?

Many staff members are also fans, and as such, they are invested personally as well as professionally. City are a big club and a major employer, but since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, the club's owners have done a good job of creating a family feel and a sense of shared purpose. More than 700 employees attended a UK all-staff meeting in the first week of this three-week international break, while players are away on duty with their national teams.

There is, however, a cloud hanging over the CFA, and the mood in general has been described to ESPN as nervous. Soriano, in his video message to staff Tuesday, insisted it should be business as usual, but in the absence of any real information about what sanctions might follow, there's genuine worry about what the future could hold.

The same goes for the players. With many of City's senior squad away on international duty, some have had direct contact with the club, while others have not. One agent of a first-team player told ESPN that his client is "calm" about the situation and is happy with the public reassurances offered by senior executives. There is, though, an acceptance that things could change depending on the result of the appeal -- which has yet to be filed but must be lodged by the close of business Friday -- and any punishment handed down.

Player concerns

Speculation over considerable sporting sanctions is causing the most concern, sources tell ESPN. After all, City's players chose to go to the Etihad Stadium to play in the Premier League and the Champions League while getting the opportunity to win trophies. articles.headline: Colts and Commanders try to build on Week 3 wins when they face each other in London
articles.description: Last November, the Indianapolis Colts went to Europe and came home with an 8-2 record. They'd beaten Atlanta in Berlin and seemed on a glide...
articles.body:
Last November, the Indianapolis Colts went to Europe and came home with an 8-2 record. They'd beaten Atlanta in Berlin and seemed on a glide path to some sort of postseason berth.


              It turned out to be their last victory of the season.


              Before too long, quarterback Daniel Jones was hurt, and the bottom fell out during a seven-game skid. Now another international game is on Indy's schedule — this time in London against the Washington Commanders on Sunday.


              “I think we try to keep these guys on a normal schedule,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said earlier this week. “So get the rest on the plane during the red-eye flight right there, and then we have a walkthrough Friday practice there. Don’t want to get out on the field right away, going on a long trip like that, and run those guys — because I’ve been a part of that where guys have stepped on the field Friday and gotten hamstrings.”


              Both teams should be familiar with the challenges of playing overseas. Washington went to Spain last season and lost to Miami. Quarterback Jayden Daniels missed that game and was replaced by Marcus Mariota. The same could happen this year in London, but Daniels has been able to practice after missing last weekend's win over Seattle because of a dislocated elbow.


              “Just taking it day by day,” he said Thursday, offering few hints about his likelihood of playing.


              Both teams should feel as if they can take advantage of this matchup. The Colts (1-2) had to open the season with games against Baltimore, Kansas City and Houston. They took the Chiefs to overtime and then beat the Texans. Only one of their next five games is at home, however, so this neutral site matchup feels pivotal.


              Washington (1-2) appeared to be in a dire situation when Daniels went down in Week 2, but Mariota led the Commanders to a victory over Seattle in their home opener last weekend. With Daniels on the mend and the Colts and New York Giants up next on the schedule, there's reason for newfound hope.


              “Obviously Marcus means a lot. Grew up, and he hates when I say this, but grew up a fan of Marcus, obviously at Oregon and in Tennessee and stuff like that,” Daniels said. “But just being around him, just the type of person he is and how much he shows that he cares about me and wants me to be at my best and anything I need, he’s really out there for me.”


              Need to know
              Indianapolis (1-2) vs. Washington (1-2) in London.

              Latest odds: Colts by 4.

              Last meeting: Commanders beat the Colts 17-16 on Oct. 30, 2022, in Indianapolis.


              Series record: Colts lead 21-11.

articles.headline: NFL Week 4 uniforms: Browns wearing 'Alpha Dawg' look; Giants go 'Legacy'
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 4, led by an alternate look from the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
As the calendar turns to October, NFL uniforms remain as fresh as ever with an alternate-heavy slate in Week 4. 

On "Thursday Night Football," the Cleveland Browns will wear their "Alpha Dawg" combination against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cleveland revealed the all-brown threads in July 2025 with a brand new alternate brown helmet. They debuted last season and marked the first time in franchise history that a brown helmet was worn. Orange-colored numbers run across the front and back of the jersey, as well as on the shoulder. There's also an orange stripe on the helmet.

In the throwback space, the New York Giants are donning their legacy uniforms against the Arizona Cardinals. New York wore these threads from 1980 to 1999. It was reintroduced in 2022, when the team brought back the navy helmet. Other design elements include classic numbers plus the red-and-blue trim on the jerseys and pants, similar to the uniforms of the 1980s and '90s. Written inside the collar is "Once a Giants, Always a Giant," the words of late owner Wellington Mara. 

The Carolina Panthers, meanwhile, will bring an all-black look to "Sunday Night Football" against the Detroit Lions. Carolina first debuted this all-black combination in 2022. 

The Dallas Cowboys are rocking navy blue alternates with silver pants against the Houston Texans, a look the team will wear only a handful of times each season. The Texans will wear liberty white jerseys with deep steel blue pants. It marks the same uniform matchup the Texans and Cowboys wore for Houston's first regular-season game as a franchise in 2002. 

The New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Falcons on Monday will honor the 20th anniversary of the Saints' return to the Superdome following Hurricane Katrina by wearing the same uniform combinations they wore for the emotional and memorable "Monday Night Football" matchup on Sept. 25, 2006. The Saints will wear white jerseys and gold pants, and the Falcons will be in their red jerseys and white pants.

articles.headline: 76ers envision LeBron James' role being 'offense creator'
articles.description: Sixers coach Nick Nurse envisions LeBron James setting the table for the offense this season. "I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said.
articles.headlineJa: 76ers、レブロン・ジェームズの役割を「オフェンスの創造者」と構想
articles.descriptionJa: シクサーズのニック・ナースHCは、今季レブロン・ジェームズがお膳立て役を担うことを見込んでいます。「私は彼を素晴らしいオフェンスの創造者だと考えている」とナースHCは語りました。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- It took until Day 3 of training camp for Philadelphia 76ers coach Nick Nurse to introduce offensive schemes to his new group.

And though the offense flowed with expected ease Thursday during 5-on-0 drills, role definition will be as important as understanding the playbook when the real games start.

Nurse detailed the offensive responsibilities he envisions LeBron James occupying. The team will certainly put the ball in the 24-year veteran's capable hands -- as, team sources told ESPN, Philadelphia discussed playing James at point forward this offseason -- but he won't be the only one with the ball.

"We got several guys that what I would call 'grab-and-go,'" Nurse said. "If they get rebounds and their first advantage is to start pushing it up the floor and it stays that way, then they're going to do it."

Beyond James, the group Nurse will rely on to push the team in transition includes fellow starters Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Though Nurse emphasized defense during the first two days of camp, part of the presentation was imploring his players to get stops to spark fast-break opportunities when scoring will come instinctively.

When the Sixers set up in the half court, however, Nurse is glad to have James, who ranks No. 1 in all-time points and No. 4 in all-time assists on this team.

"I just think LeBron, I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said. "I don't necessarily mean scorer, I just think creator and a table setter and all that kind of stuff. ... If it isn't bringing it up and starting [the possession], it's probably going to be first pass anyway to [him on] the wing and then we get into our actions, and he's kind of seeing what's there, and he's creating offense for others."

As the Sixers look to organize themselves against a set defense, that's when player recognition will be paramount.

James, Brown and Joel Embiid, for instance, can operate out of the post to initiate offense. The court, however, can get awfully crowded if the team has a player planted on either block and any of those three expect their touches there.

"One, it's a feel thing, and two, we just try to establish some spacing," Brown said. "We try to establish position on the floor, like the style of play. I think we're still kind of figuring it out. Like when I am going to go, when not to go, when big fella is going down in the post, when I can put pressure on the rim, just trying to find that balance."

Brown has already spent time with coaches after practice this week, not only practicing fadeaway shots when double-teamed in the post, but also practicing throwing passes to the 3-point line to elude the double.

Sixers player development coaches have been the recipients of those passes, but the idea is for Brown to picture finding one of his star teammates open if he dissects the defense properly.

"I played with a fair share of stretch 5s, and it really complements my game well," Brown said of Embiid.

articles.body:
Week 4 of the NFL season has arrived, and the calendar has officially flipped to October. But sweater weather hasn't quite followed everywhere. 

Unseasonable heat out West could keep layers light for another week, while cooler temperatures settling in across the East are opening the door for more fall-ready fits. That means players have plenty of options as they make their Week 4 entrances. With three weeks of looks already in the books, personal styles are also starting to take shape around the league. Some players have leaned into statement pieces, while others have kept things clean and understated.

From warm-weather looks to seasonal layers, Week 4 brings another round of game-day style as the calendar officially turns to fall.

Thursday night's fashion

Players and coaches aren't the only ones showing off their style pregame. Mascots get in on the tunnel fits, too. This week, Brownie the Elf was ready to rock for Cleveland's Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Game, channeling Prince in a purple jacket with a matching guitar.

articles.headline: Brian Flores and his dominant Vikings defense take on the winless Dolphins, the team he once coached
articles.description: — Brian Flores has become one of the most impactful and prominent assistant coaches in the
articles.headlineJa: ブライアン・フローレス率いる強力なバイキングス守備陣が、古巣である未勝利のドルフィンズと対戦
articles.descriptionJa: — ブライアン・フローレスは、最も影響力があり目立った活躍を見せるアシスタントコーチのひとりとなっています。
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Brian Flores has become one of the most impactful and prominent assistant coaches in the NFL over four seasons as defensive coordinator of the Minnesota Vikings, with his knack for play calling and a gift for maximizing the group's strengths.


              Flores might be doing his best work yet this year with the undefeated Vikings, who have allowed the second-fewest points in the league. He'll have the opportunity on Sunday to show off his tricks to his old team, the winless Miami Dolphins.


              Fired after a three-season run as their head coach, Flores sued the NFL a month later in allegation of racially discriminatory hiring practices in a landmark case that's still in the court system four years later and awaits a trial sometime in 2027. Even if the Dolphins roster has only two players left from his last team in 2021 and his replacement Mike McDaniel was fired after last season, owner Stephen Ross remains in control of the club.


              If Flores has any strong feelings about facing the Dolphins, though, he's keeping those to himself, other than an eagerness to catch up before the game with the dozens of support staffers he's still friendly with.


              “I'm the same every week,” Flores said. “It's never about me. It's always about our team, and so the preparation's going to be the same.”


              The Vikings defense has been especially ready this season, with league-best rates in sacks per pass attempt, touchdowns allowed inside the 20-yard line, and third down conversions. The foundation for Flores has long begun with an unwavering trust in his players.


              “I tell them all the time, when people turn on the Vikings, I hope they see a team that really is connected and is having fun playing ball," Flores said. “I think we're doing that.”


              The Dolphins, with star running back De'Vone Achane done for the season with a torn ACL and quarterback Malik Willis making just his 10th career start, will have a tough task amid the deafening roar of the crowd at U.S. Bank Stadium in trying to identify and block all those creative and unpredictable sets and rushes.


              “You just can’t get really scared of it," rookie guard Kadyn Proctor said. "Just have to be locked in to the slants and to the blitzes and really just focus on doing our one-eleventh, focus on our job.”


              Need to know
              Miami (0-3) at Minnesota (3-0).


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:05 p.m. EDT, CBS.


              Latest odds: Vikings by 10½.


              Against the spread: Dolphins 0-3; Vikings 3-0.


              Last week: Dolphins lost to the Chiefs 24-10; Vikings beat the Buccaneers 23-16.


              Last meeting: Vikings beat the Dolphins 24-16 on Oct. 16, 2022, in Miami. 


              Series record: Dolphins lead 8-6.


              Matchup to watch
              Vikings OLB Dallas Turner vs. Dolphins LT Patrick Paul.

articles.headline: Burrow seeks to stay unbeaten vs Lawrence as Bengals host Jaguars in matchup of 2-1 teams
articles.description: Joe Burrow has gotten the better of Trevor Lawrence whenever their teams have met.
articles.headlineJa: 2勝1敗同士が激突、ベンガルズがジャガーズを迎え撃つ中でバロウはローレンス相手の無敗維持を狙う
articles.descriptionJa: ジョー・バロウは、チーム同士が対戦するたびにトレバー・ローレンスを上回る成績を収めています。
articles.body:
Joe Burrow has gotten the better of Trevor Lawrence whenever their teams have met. 


              Burrow is hoping that trend continues on Sunday when his Cincinnati Bengals host Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in a matchup of 2-1 teams.


              Burrow is 3-0 in starts against Lawrence. The first was in the College Football Playoff national title game in the 2019 season when he threw for 463 yards and accounted for all six touchdowns in LSU's 42-25 victory over Clemson.


              The most recent time Burrow faced the Jaguars though is one he would like to forget. The franchise quarterback suffered a turf toe injury during the second quarter of last season's Week 2 game while being sacked by Jaguars defensive tackle Arik Armstead.


              Even though the Bengals rallied for a 31-27 victory behind Jake Browning, Burrow missed the next nine games after having surgery on his left big toe. The Bengals season imploded as they lost eight of nine.


              Burrow's focus though is making sure Cincinnati gets back on track after a loss at Pittsburgh despite passing for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Cincinnati was in Steelers' territory during the fourth quarter when Burrow fumbled after being sacked by Derrick Harmon.


              Burrow will face a Jaguars defense that is second in pressure rate this season.


              “They’re deep. Their two edge rushers — Armstead and DaVon (Hamilton) are really good. All those guys can play really good football, get pressure on the quarterback, stop the run,” Burrow said. “Then the rest of their defense plays with their roles really well, understands what they’re trying to do with their coverages.”


              The Jaguars' defense has picked off a pass in eight straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL, and has allowed a league-low 36 points this season.


              Cincinnati's defense also has plenty of questions going into the game. After strong games against Tampa Bay and Houston, the Bengals reverted back to the level of the past couple of seasons against the Steelers with missed tackles and lapses on long pass plays.


              Lawrence has 65 completions of at least 20 yards since the start of last season, third most in the AFC. The Bengals allowed five last week.


              “Things have changed and I think they’ve figured out kind of what they’re good at. And in some ways I think it’s kind of simplified," Lawrence said of the Bengals, the only AFC team he hasn't defeated.


              "I think sometimes that’s the hardest thing to go against is a really well-coached defense that might not bring a ton of pressures and all those things and have guys running free, but they’re just always in the right spot at the right time and you got to really earn every run, every completion, all those things. I think they’re doing a good job of that right now.”
